## 37ef814e99dd

**Reproduced possible shortcut / validator-domain mismatch.** The canonical program keeps the actual 4-neighbor boundary of each object. Current production emitted 1,464/1,464 sampled components as solid rectangles across 600 draws, so the shortcut “replace each object with the full perimeter of its bounding box” is indistinguishable on that production domain. The current `self_check` nevertheless accepts a concave L-shaped object.

The exact accepted input, canonical Racket output, bbox-perimeter rival, seven differing cells, source hashes, and 600-draw probe are in `checks/audit/37ef814e99dd/analysis.json`; the supported Racket receipt is `checks/audit/37ef814e99dd/racket.json`. Generator SHA-256: `290424e3332b0eea7380544a46e5ca0d9112dc94910499477b933431bb644a26`; rule hash: `509691e53ef9`.

The counterexample passes the current validator (`self_check == []`) but is outside the documented solid-rectangle generator domain. The generator does not emit such cases in the sampled domain. Recommended resolution: either make the validator enforce the documented rectangle-only domain and state that the bbox shortcut is intentionally equivalent there, or broaden production with lawful nonrectangular objects and teach the true object-boundary rule. No audit-target files were changed.
